A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, four figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including the expanded proofs in v4.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original logistic-regression experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Appendix G.3 reports original numerical inversion-bias experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains the original logistic-regression and inversion-bias experiments in Section 5 and Appendix G.3.

M1.justification: The sampling reweighting in Equation (5), scalar debiasing, approximate-leverage variants, and SSN updates remain unchanged. The revised theoretical guarantees do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate logistic regression and inversion bias using MNIST and CIFAR-10. Appendix G retains the same binary grouping of image classes; no dataset or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Newton-LESS in Figure 2; GD, SGD, LESS, SRHT, ARLev, ALev, and SLev in Figure 3; and RLev, ARLev, DARLev with their non-debiased counterparts in Figure 4.

E3.justification: Empirical settings remain unchanged, including dataset dimensions, preprocessing, regularization, timing conventions, Figure 2's five/seven iterations, and Figure 3's sketch sizes of 300/400. Revised theoretical sample-size requirements are not changes to the experiments.

E4.justification: The sketch-size sweep in Figure 2 and Appendix G.3's comparisons of exact versus approximate leverage sampling, with and without scalar debiasing, are retained without additional ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Figures 2, 3, and 4 retain averaging over 30, 10, and 500 independent runs, respectively, with deterministic GD excepted. No empirical uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 2–4 retain the same numerical curves, comparisons, and reported findings, including ARLev's favorable convergence–time tradeoff and reduced inversion bias under scalar debiasing. The theoretical bound revisions are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Lemma A.4 replaces Burkholder's inequality with a martingale Rosenthal inequality. Lemma D.1 replaces an individual variance bound with an expected-maximum bound using moments of order log(n), correcting the expectation/maximum step in Appendix D.2. The resulting log(n)/log(log(n)) factor propagates through Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.2, and Appendices E–F, changing sample-size requirements, bias bounds, and SSN convergence errors and neighborhoods.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same central claims: characterizing and correcting inversion bias for random sampling and SRHT, and establishing problem-independent local SSN convergence. Their high-level scope is unchanged despite the revised quantitative guarantees.

C2.justification: Remark 3.5 incorporates logarithmic factors into the threshold determining when scalar debiasing matches fine-grained debiasing, changing that applicability boundary. The two-regime interpretation, empirical explanations, and future-work limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same leverage-score and SJLT construction details, Armijo line search, preprocessing, regularization parameters, and reference to the Newton-LESS repository. No implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes Burkholder (1973) and adds de la Peña and Giné (1999) for the replacement martingale inequality. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The document retains its organization and most prose, with local proof expansion, added tilde asymptotic notation, and an updated date. Numerous cross-references now incorrectly say Theorem while their targets remain labeled Definition, Lemma, Proposition, Remark, or Assumption.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes its asymptotic axis annotations to include tilde-O and tilde-Theta. Figures 2–4 retain their plots and panel structures; revised equations and text cause local reflow and changes in placement relative to surrounding paragraphs.

improvement.justification: V3's Equation (27) unjustifiably moves a maximum outside an expectation. V4's Equation (28) retains the expected maximum and supplies a high-moment argument in Lemma D.1, propagating its logarithmic cost into the central guarantees. Addressing this foundational proof gap substantially improves the mathematical support for this primarily theoretical paper. The more conservative bounds reflect that correction; the introduced cross-reference errors are a smaller presentation drawback.
